chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Naw ibn Ibrahim, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had a man testify in his presence, and his hand and leg had been cut off due to his testimony, so he accepted his testimony, and he had repented and his repentance was known.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ يَدُهُ وَ رِجْلُهُ: His hand and leg were cut (penal punishment)

ai.seo_question: Does a person whose hand and leg have been cut for slander retain the right to testify?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) validates the testimony of a man who had undergone *hadd* punishment for slander (*qadhf*), ruling that the physical penalty does not permanently strip one of legal capacity (*ahliyyah*) if repentance (*tawbah*) is established. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that *hadd* punishments serve to purify the individual rather than permanently disqualify them from bearing witness, provided their repentance is known and accepted. The case underscores the importance of distinguishing between the penalty for a specific act and the ongoing moral integrity of the witness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, a man testified in his<sup>asws</sup> presence with a testimony, and his hand and his leg had been cut. So he<sup>asws</sup> allowed his testimony, and he had repented and his repentance had been recognised’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, accepted the testimony of a man whose hand and foot was cut off, he had repented and his repentance had become known . 555
